purpose: Curated plant-health evidence registry for dr-plant. Records are references and research leads, not diagnostic training labels unless explicitly validated.

rules.promotion: A finding may be used as diagnostic evidence only after expert review, symptom verification, image provenance and license checks.
rules.socialMedia: Social-media posts are leads only. Never treat captions or comments as confirmed diagnoses.
rules.images: Do not copy or redistribute images until their license or explicit permission is verified.
rules.uncertainty: Keep suspected, reported, and confirmed findings separate.

sources.title: Texas A&M AgriLife – Powdery Mildew (Erysiphe necator) in Grapes (July 2026)

diseases.notes: Differential-diagnosis reference. A 2025 study from Sweida in southern Syria reported isolation of Phomopsis viticola from symptomatic grapevine samples collected during 2020–2022; confirm current accepted taxonomy and local coastal occurrence separately. This is Syrian evidence, but not evidence from Latakia or Tartous.

sources.title: University of Minnesota Extension – Grape leaf spots
El-Halabi et al. (2025) – Spread of Dead-Arm Disease on Grapevine Caused by Phomopsis viticola in Southern Syria

diseases.notes: A peer-reviewed first report documented a 2006 survey and serological testing in Syrian citrus-growing areas including Jableh and other locations in Latakia, and sites in Tartous. Treat this as a historical published regional record, not a statement about present-day prevalence or any particular tree. Symptoms alone are insufficient; laboratory testing is required.

datasets.name: Grapevine Bunch Images with Powdery Mildew Severity Labels Collected under Field Conditions
datasets.intendedUse: Candidate for separate bunch-level symptom/severity research; do not mix bunch images with leaf-image classes without explicit task labels and separate evaluation.
datasets.notes: Published 13 October 2026. Images were captured in situ during the 2023 fruiting season in one commercial vineyard in Bouarg, Nador Province, northeastern Morocco. Labels describe visible bunch symptoms and are image-level ordinal grades, not laboratory-confirmed infection measurements. One vineyard and one season limit generalization. Mendeley record lists CC BY 4.0; preserve creator attribution and dataset citation.

datasets.name: Grapevine Leaves RGB Images of Disease Symptoms (North Portugal, 2024–2025)
datasets.region: Four vineyard sites in northern Portugal (Vila Real and Ponte de Lima)
datasets.intendedUse: High-priority candidate for a separate field grape-leaf classification baseline after downloading the archive, verifying the Zenodo record's own license and file integrity, auditing labels and near-duplicates, and building location/date-aware train/validation/test splits.
datasets.license: The Data in Brief article is CC BY 4.0; the Zenodo dataset record's own license and file-level terms have not yet been independently verified.
datasets.notes: The paper reports 1,122 healthy, 1,006 downy mildew, 1,126 powdery mildew, 1,000 Esca complex, and 1,013 erineum mite images. Images were collected in natural vineyard conditions across four sites and two growing seasons using a Redmi Note 12 Pro. A second reviewer performed final annotation quality control. Dataset is geographically Mediterranean but not Syrian; performance transfer to coastal Syria must be evaluated independently. Do not treat paper-reported accuracy as Dr Plant performance.
